study_metadata.title: CycloneLM Phase 7: Pretrained Model Comparison Matrix
study_metadata.project: CYCLONE INTEL — Coastal Karnataka Cyclone Preparedness
study_metadata.hardware_target: Intel Core i5-13500H CPU (12 cores, 16 threads, AVX2, AVX-VNNI), 16 GB RAM (12 GiB usable), Intel Iris Xe iGPU, Ubuntu Linux
study_metadata.constraint_summary: Zero-cost, open-weights, no paid APIs, no credit card required, strict CPU training & inference feasibility

candidate_models.architecture: Custom Decoder-only Transformer (Post-LN, learned absolute embeddings)
cons: Severe data starvation (220:1 param-to-token ratio)
0.0% Pydantic valid JSON tool calling
Cannot generate fluent English syntax or reasoning from scratch
Prone to limit-cycle repetition without penalty
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: Preserve as experimental reference baseline; discontinue for conversational and assistant production tasks.

candidate_models.architecture: Distilled GPT-2 (6 layers, 12 heads, 768 hidden, Post-LN)
cons: Distilled in 2019 without instruction fine-tuning
Outdated architecture (Post-LN, absolute positional embeddings)
Very weak structured output adherence and reasoning
Small 1024 context window
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: Not recommended. Lacks instruction alignment; substantially outperformed by modern sub-500M architectures.

pros: High library compatibility and ubiquitous examples
cons: Pretrained in 2019 on uncurated web text (WebText)
No instruction tuning or alignment
Lacks modern LLM architectural enhancements (RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU)
Hallucinates heavily when prompted for structured evidence synthesis
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: Not recommended. Superseded across all quality, efficiency, and safety dimensions by modern models.

candidate_models.architecture: Llama-derived modern decoder (30 layers, 9 heads, 3 KV heads [GQA], 576 hidden, RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU)
pros: Pretrained on 11 trillion high-quality educational tokens (FineWeb-Edu, Cosmopedia v2)
Pre-aligned with DPO and SFT for instruction following
High CPU generation speed (80.7 tokens/s on i5-13500H)
8k context window allows multi-turn evidence context
Both full fine-tuning and LoRA fit within available laptop RAM
cons: Limited parameter capacity for complex multi-step reasoning
Small hidden dimension (576) can lead to slight compression loss on technical domain terms
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: Excellent candidate for edge deployment, lightweight CPU serving, and low-latency response generation.

candidate_models.architecture: Llama-derived modern decoder (32 layers, 15 heads, 5 KV heads [GQA], 960 hidden, RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU)
pros: High linguistic fluency and syntactic consistency
LoRA fine-tuning comfortably fits in 1.3 GB RAM
CPU inference throughput of ~20 tokens/sec is well above human reading speed
cons: Full fine-tuning on CPU (6.8 GB RAM) is tight on 5.3 GB free memory; must use LoRA
Slightly smaller community adoption than Qwen2.5 series
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: Strong candidate. Excellent balance between parameter expressiveness and CPU resource utilization.

candidate_models.architecture: Qwen2 modern decoder (24 layers, 14 heads, 2 KV heads [GQA], 896 hidden, intermediate 4864, RMSNorm, RoPE)
pros: Permissive Apache 2.0 license, un-gated, free open weights
Industry-standard benchmark leader for models under 1B parameters
Massive 152k vocabulary provides superior tokenization of technical and geographic terms
Superior instruction following, schema awareness, and factual grounding
LoRA fine-tuning uses only 1.8 GB RAM on CPU
Inference runs smoothly at 20.3 tokens/sec on i5-13500H CPU
cons: Full fine-tuning requires 9.1 GB RAM (exceeds available free RAM, necessitating LoRA)
Embedding table represents ~136M params due to large 152k vocabulary
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: PRIMARY RECOMMENDATION. Best empirical instruction following, evidence synthesis quality, and safety alignment under 1B parameters.

candidate_models.architecture: Qwen2 modern decoder (28 layers, 12 heads, 2 KV heads [GQA], 1536 hidden, intermediate 8960)
pros: Highest reasoning quality among sub-2B models
cons: Full fine-tuning on CPU impossible (>26 GB RAM needed)
LoRA training requires ~5.8 GB RAM (exceeds current 5.3 GB available memory, risking thrashing)
CPU inference latency drops to ~6.8 tokens/sec, causing sluggish interactive UX
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: Not recommended for this laptop hardware. Exceeds practical CPU training budget.

candidate_models.provider: Zhang et al. / Singapore University of Technology and Design
candidate_models.architecture: Llama-2 architecture (22 layers, 32 heads, 4 KV heads, 2048 hidden)
cons: Outperformed across benchmarks by Qwen2.5-0.5B despite having 2.2x parameters
Small 2048 context window
Heavy memory consumption during training (~4.5 GB LoRA)
Inferior instruction adherence compared to SmolLM2 and Qwen2.5
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: Not recommended. Superseded by Qwen2.5-0.5B and SmolLM2 series.

candidate_models.architecture: Llama-3.2 modern decoder (16 layers, 32 heads, 8 KV heads, 2048 hidden, 128k context)
cons: Requires manual Hugging Face account approval and gated license acceptance
Non-standard Llama 3.2 community license restrictions
LoRA training is marginal on 5.3 GB available RAM (~5.0 GB needed)
CPU inference speed is relatively slow (<9 tokens/s)
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: Disqualified due to gated access requirements, proprietary licensing constraints, and memory overhead.

candidate_models.architecture: Bidirectional BERT encoder (6 layers, 12 heads, 384 hidden)
pros: 100% deterministic argmax intent routing over 7 tools + refusal class
0.0% syntax failure risk (cannot generate malformed JSON)
Can be fine-tuned or trained with SetFit in under 2 minutes on CPU
cons: Cannot perform free-text natural-language generation (encoder only)
Must be paired with a generative model for synthesis
candidate_models.recommendation_notes: PRIMARY RECOMMENDATION FOR INTENT ROUTING. Solves the 0.0% tool calling failure mode deterministically.

natural_language_generation.justification: Highest instruction adherence, 32k context, 152k vocab, Apache 2.0, viable for CPU LoRA fine-tuning and 20 tokens/s CPU inference.
Fastest CPU inference (80.7 tokens/s), minimal RAM footprint (<300 MB), 8k context, Apache 2.0, ultra-efficient for laptop deployment.
Solid middle ground between 135M and 0.5B, good fluency, viable with LoRA.

tool_intent_routing.justification: Deterministic classification head over 7 tools + refusal; eliminates autoregressive JSON syntax errors entirely (<10ms CPU latency).
Can perform schema-aware generation, but autoregressive generation remains vulnerable to syntax errors compared to a dedicated classifier.
